states.narration: What is being counted? Both terms count copies of the same whole quantity x+3.
Combine the two counts while keeping their shared group intact. Nothing inside x+3 changes.
Two copies and three copies make five copies. Only the count has been evaluated.
Where does each contribution go? Every one of the five copies contains both x and 3, so both receive the factor five.
The five constant contributions total fifteen. The five copies of x remain; no contribution is lost.

editorial.title: How do we regroup without losing any contributions?
editorial.setup: Read multiplication as counting copies. First count the repeated whole group, then open it to track each contribution.
editorial.summary: Collect the counts, preserve the group, then apply the combined count to every term inside. These equalities preserve the value even when x+3 is zero.
